隋書卷七十二列傳第三十七 is a volume and biography-section heading; the prior English invents ordinal years and is ungrammatical. Volume 72, Biographies 37 matches the Chinese.
Moreover, this boy will win fame and office early in life, yet his years will not exceed sixty or seventy."
Moreover, this boy will win fame and office early in life, yet his years will not exceed six times seven (forty-two)."
壽不過六七 is verified by s0110 終於四十二，六七之言，於是驗矣, so 六七 is six times seven (forty-two), not a sixty-to-seventy range.
Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed sixty or seventy."
Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed six times seven (forty-two)."
The same prophetic 六七 is fulfilled at age forty-two in s0110; sixty or seventy cannot be the intended sense in this multiplicative riddle.
He later died at forty-two, and the monk's words about sixty or seventy were thus fulfilled.
He later died at forty-two, and the monk's words about six times seven were thus fulfilled.
終於四十二 proves that 六七之言 means six-times-seven, so reporting the monk's words as sixty or seventy contradicts the Chinese fulfillment.
Later he died at forty-two; the words about sixty or seventy were thus fulfilled.
Later he died at forty-two; the words 'six times seven' were thus fulfilled.
六七之言 paired with death at forty-two requires the multiplicative reading; sixty or seventy is not supported.
